sources.full: Chaos at the Food Court: Modern Earth

adventure.name: Chaos at the Food Court: Modern Earth
adventure.author: Offscreen Worlds, adapted from the 2019 C2E2 premise

contents.name: 01 - Maps
headers: Build EAST - Food Court and Coronet

contents.name: 03 - Concourse, Looking Glass Games and Food Court

entries.name: Adventure in Brief
entries: Four level-8 adventurers investigating strange lights at Thornwatch enter a modern shopping mall through a cinema screen. Elias's crystal projector opened secondary rifts, releasing eight monsters. Each living escaped monster inside the building sustains a strand of arcane energy; the screen cannot become a stable doorway home until all active strands end.

WEST contains the cinema, Hydra and security. The 450-foot connecting concourse passes Looking Glass Games before reaching EAST: food court, Owlbear stockrooms, and the Young Red Dragon's hoard in Coronet Jewelers. Eddie Vale's attempted theft may bring the dragon out of the shop.

entries.name: What Happened
entries: Elias Trask owns Looking Glass Games midway along the main mall concourse. He bought an antique crystal projector at an estate sale; earlier tests produced strange light and humming near Thornwatch's arch. During a promotional fantasy-film screening at the West cinema, he switched it on, saw it overload and fled to his shop.

The projector connected the cinema screen to Thornwatch, bringing the party through its primary doorway. Secondary tears released eight creatures: one Hydra, two Displacer Beasts, one Gelatinous Cube, one Spectator, two Owlbears, and one Young Red Dragon. All eight arrived before the party, with no later monster arrivals.

Each living escaped creature maintains a planar strand while inside the mall building, including its roof. Dying, going off-plane, or exiting the building disconnects it; returning alive inside the mall reconnects it. An unconscious creature remains linked. The adventurers crossed by the primary screen and carry no strand.

Eight violet strands glow inside the projector crystal. A strand dims when its creature disconnects. Rotating the crystal reveals the general direction of each surviving strand. DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana) identifies their planar resonance.

STOP halts the electrical motor but the crystal beam continues while any strand remains. With no active strands, STOP opens the cinema screen to Thornwatch for one minute (immediately if already stopped). An intact projector can be cycled for later openings; a shattered crystal cannot.

The dragon has claimed Coronet Jewelers as its hoard and is not allied to the others. Two Owlbears forage in separate kitchen/service stockrooms, trapped behind security shutters lowered during evacuation. Two Displacer Beasts, a Spectator and a Gelatinous Cube roam the East food court independently.

Eddie Vale hides beside Coronet's shattered storefront. He attempts to steal a tray of watches after the immediate food-court predators are no longer attacking nearby. If he escapes with it, the dragon pursues the treasure; if he is intercepted, the dragon stays with its hoard unless otherwise threatened.

entries.name: Table Coordinates and Pieces
entries: WEST folding mat: 22×26 squares; cinema booth C3–E4, security P3–U9, fountain I12–O18. EAST rolled mat: 34×22 squares; Coronet X2–AG8, food court and service kitchens. A1 is upper left; 5 feet per square. Looking Glass Games stands halfway along the 450-foot connecting concourse.

entries.caption: Creature placements by map
rows: In hoard; reacts to robbery or intrusion

entries.name: Target Session Flow
entries: Session target: about 3–4 hours, including changing maps and player decisions. Suggested time ranges, NOT mandatory timers: Thornwatch/cinema 10–20 minutes, Hydra 20–35, security and Looking Glass Games 15–25, food court 30–45, east-mall finale 35–60, ending 5–15. Actual timing varies.

Eight escaped monsters in three encounter opportunities: Hydra; two Displacer Beasts, Gelatinous Cube and Spectator; then two Owlbears and Young Red Dragon. Creatures are independently motivated, not a coordinated team. No Bulette, Mimics, or automatic monster reinforcements.

DM controls dramatic entrances consistent with the scene. A shutter can crash open when repeated blows finally buckle it, including during the dragon scene, without counting each Owlbear swing. Player efforts to brace, repair, open or magically hold it must still matter. The DM controls events, not player outcomes.

entries.name: Miniature Pull List - Numbered Catalog
entries: PACK EIGHT MONSTER FIGURES TOTAL, taken from your numbered Arcknight 161-figure catalog. The catalog numbers are personal inventory IDs, not Monster Manual numbers. Each row names its exact binder pocket. Proxy figures represent the monster using the correct rules footprint; an exact creature-type match may still have an oversized physical model.

entries.caption: Eight monster figures and binder locations
rows: #159 Red Dragon (exact creature type; oversized figure)
Large 2×2 marker; place physical figure nearby if overhangs

entries: OPTIONAL: Eddie Vale is catalog #069 Red-coated Bandit/NPC, P09 Back TL, Medium 1×1, only if you need to track his position in initiative. The catalog description is provisional. No miniatures are needed for security guard Dana Torres, usher Mel Ruiz, shopkeeper Elias Trask, or fleeing civilians.
Players bring their own player-character miniatures. None are part of your preparation inventory. The DM brings eight monster figures, and at most one optional NPC figure.

Footprint plates/markers: one Huge 3×3 (Hydra), six Large 2×2 (both Displacers, Cube, two Owlbears, Dragon), and one Medium 1×1 (Spectator), using existing bases where possible. The large #159 Red Dragon figure must occupy only a 2×2 battle footprint despite the oversized plastic.

entries.name: Player and DM PNG Images
entries: WEST and EAST are connected by a 450-foot, 30-foot-wide enclosed shopping concourse with ordinary fire doors and turns. Looking Glass Games is on its north wall, 225 feet from either end. West connects at V12–V16 to East at A10–C14.
WEST: Cinema east entrance, booth door into theater, and west-side security door are marked. Fountain water is shallow difficult terrain for creatures without Swim Speed; its rim may grant cover.

EAST: Eye Express and ThunderCube are ordinary retail stores. The Cube begins outside the west kitchen doorway (M19–N20); Owlbear O1 starts behind a jammed service shutter (G19–H20). Coronet's broken south frontage at AB8–AD8 opens into the food court. The atrium ceiling is 35 feet; balconies are 15 feet high.

EAST SHUTTERS (now drawn on both map images): the west kitchen's east-side opening at the L/M boundary, rows 19–22, is entirely blocked by a 20-foot-wide jammed rolling security shutter. The east service room's 10-foot north opening along AB16–AC16 is blocked by a second jammed shutter. These are real barriers; there is no open side passage bypassing either shutter. Each is AC 19, 100 HP, and can be opened or destroyed.

entries.name: Build WEST - Cinema and Fountain
entries: Build WEST on the 22-column × 26-row folding dry-erase mat. A1 is upper-left, 1 square = 5 feet. Use the linked WEST player PNG for all walls/doors and the DM PNG for hidden locations. Cinema B3–I9, projector booth C3–E4, security office P3–U9, shallow fountain I12–O18, concourse exit V12–V16.

Draw/place the 7×7 fountain and rim, two overturned kiosk/counter areas at approximately C16–F17 and Q15–S16, theater seats/aisles, the booth door and security room. Fountain water is difficult terrain for creatures without Swim Speed; rim provides half cover when it blocks a line of attack.

Hydra #145 stand-in starts L13–N15 on a 3×3 Huge footprint in fountain. The four arriving characters appear in the cinema near E7–H8 unless their approach changes it. Players provide their own figures; you do not pack those figures. No security guard or usher figure is needed.
West shop walls can be drawn, not constructed as separate 3D terrain. Shoppers flee off-map rather than needing tokens.

entries.name: Build EAST - Food Court and Coronet
entries: Build EAST on the 34-column × 22-row ENHANCE dry-erase mat. A1 is upper-left, 1 square = 5 feet. West approach A10–C14; ThunderCube and Eye Express on north side; west kitchen approximately C16–L22; east service room approximately Z16–AG22; Coronet Jewelers X2–AG8; east public exit AF12–AG13.

Place or draw four 2×1 food-court table/counter rectangles at M15–N15, S14–T14, W16–X16, S20–T20. Draw the closed 20-foot west-kitchen shutter along the L/M boundary for rows 19–22, and the 10-foot east-service shutter across AB–AC at the boundary between rows 15 and 16. Both shutters are already pictured on the revised player and DM PNGs.

EAST monster starts: Spectator #119 M10 at 15 feet elevation (1×1), Displacer #140 N12–O13 (2×2), Displacer #105 proxy U10–V11 (2×2), Cube #139 M19–N20 outside west kitchen (2×2), Owlbear #141 G19–H20 inside west kitchen (2×2), Owlbear #135 proxy AC19–AD20 in east service (2×2), Dragon #159 Z4–AA5 inside Coronet (2×2 even if miniature itself is oversized).

Eddie starts AE10; exposed tray of watches at AD8–AD9 outside Coronet's broken front. Broken storefront AB8–AD8. Correct east exit: AF12–AG13, NOT the earlier AG12–AH13. Eddie #069 is optional for tactical tracking.

Construct/draw: room outlines, counter/table blocks, two shutter segments, broken jewelry frontage, watch tray and the two exits. Put height markers beside the Spectator or flying dragon. No third mat is needed to represent the connecting concourse.

entries.name: Movement, Elevation and Scenery
entries: The WEST V12–V16 passage meets a 450-foot long, 30-foot wide enclosed shopping concourse ending at EAST A10–C14. Looking Glass Games is on the north side, exactly halfway along, 225 feet from each end. Narrate normal travel; sketch a six-square-wide corridor only if tactical combat begins there.

EAST atrium ceiling: 35 feet. Two upper display/maintenance gallery lips stand 15 feet above floor along the north shop fronts: ThunderCube D7–K7 and Eye Express M7–U7. Each is 5 feet deep. They can be reached by a staff stair inside the corresponding shop or by climbing (DC 13 Strength [Athletics] when uncertain). Use an elevation marker on the same mapped squares rather than a third battle map.

Shop glass: AC 13 and 10 HP per 5-foot pane, if intentionally broken. Food tables/counters are movable terrain and give half cover only where they actually obstruct attacks. No automatic cover through open areas.

entries.name: Thornwatch
entries: The reeve hired the party to investigate violet lights, low humming, and odd reflections around the old stone waystation near Thornwatch.

READ ALOUD: The road to Thornwatch winds through dark pines. For three nights, locals have reported violet lights and a low hum near the abandoned waystation. Ahead, an old stone arch gleams faintly in the still air.
Faint scorch lines cross the arch; puddles sometimes reflect an unfamiliar ceiling. DC 13 Arcana reveals planar instability.

READ ALOUD: A deep note hums through the stones. Violet light fills the arch. Your reflections lag a heartbeat. The ground drops away, and the smell of pine becomes butter, sugar, and popcorn. Your boots strike red carpet before an enormous moving picture.
The pulse draws the nearby party through to the West cinema together.

entries.name: The Thornwatch Contract
entries: PLAYER-FACING CONTRACT (contained here, no external handout needed): 'By order of the Reeve of Thornwatch: investigate the violet flashes, humming and unnatural reflections at the abandoned road arch. Determine the cause and end the disturbance. Reward: 400 gold pieces to the party upon satisfactory return and report. Signed, the Reeve of Thornwatch.'
This commission does not require the adventurers to kill monsters. If they never return, the payment may be lost; being stranded on modern Earth is a valid ending.

entries.name: The Cinema
entries: READ ALOUD: Rows of padded chairs face a wall-sized moving image. A child points at your weapons and asks, 'Are you in the movie?' A crash shakes the building; screams follow from the concourse.
Mel Ruiz, a cinema usher, is pinned under a fallen curtain bar (DC 13 Athletics, two people lifting, or suitable magic). Mel saw Elias install the projector and heard a many-headed creature outside.

Projector in CINEMA BOOTH C3–E4, reached through the door at rear of theater. STOP halts electric motor but the violet beam persists while monster links remain. Eight strands glow in the crystal; close inspection suggests each follows a living moving creature. DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana) reveals they are tethers to the escaped creatures and can be cut by death, leaving the plane, or leaving the building (including its roof). Rotating the crystal gives the general direction of each still-connected creature. The Hydra's death visibly extinguishes one strand; this also establishes the rule without requiring an Arcana success.

entries.name: Projector - What Characters Can Learn
entries: The crystal's eight violet strands correspond to eight escaped monsters. While a monster is alive and inside the mall (including its roof), its strand stays lit. Death, exiting the mall or departure from the plane disconnects it. An unconscious creature stays connected. When a disconnected living monster returns inside, its strand reignites. The adventurers entered through the primary doorway and have no strands.

STOP only turns off the motor until no strands remain. An intact crystal with zero strands permits STOP to open the cinema screen to Thornwatch for one minute; subsequent RUN/STOP cycles can reopen it. Switching the projector off or unplugging it never kills, banishes, or weakens a monster.

CRYSTAL OBJECT: treat the magic crystal as a resilient Small glass object: AC 13, 10 HP, immune to Poison and Psychic damage. Smashing it destroys this portal's means of reopening; the characters can be stranded on Earth, and all monsters remain wherever they are. The motor can be disabled independently without breaking the crystal; doing so does not end the violet magic.
DISPEL MAGIC (2024): the crystal's dimensional resonance is an innate magic-item property, not an ongoing spell. Dispel Magic does not shut the device down, sever strands or remove escaped creatures.

BANISHMENT (2024): a banished creature's strand goes dark while it is away. A creature returning inside the mall reconnects. If the spell lasts a full minute, only an Aberration, Celestial, Elemental, Fey or Fiend stays banished under the 2024 spell. In this roster the Spectator is an Aberration and may be permanently banished; the others return after the spell ends. Apply the spell's normal save and Concentration requirements.

The eight threads are visible from the first scene, and the Hydra provides the first demonstration. Never make Elias or a successful check the sole source of the explanation. The characters may elect to stay on Earth even if the screen reopens.

entries.name: Encounter 1: Hydra
entries: READ ALOUD: Five reptilian heads sweep above a shattered fountain rim. The enormous creature thrashes in the water as shoppers flee between overturned kiosks.

WEST L13–N15: Hydra (184 HP), already at the fountain I12–O18. It snaps at nearby movement and pursues armed threats past the overturned kiosks. On death, a violet arc fades and one projector strand goes dark.

DM PHYSICAL SETUP: Hydra mini catalog #145 (Chimera proxy) on 3×3 marker at L13–N15, fountain I12–O18. Use linked 2024 Hydra stat block for heads and Fire; its death turns off one projector strand visibly.
{@creature Hydra|XMM}

data.name: 03 - Concourse, Looking Glass Games and Food Court

entries.name: Dana Torres and the Concourse
entries: Dana Torres manages mall security and coordinates the evacuation from WEST security (P3–U9). Her cameras recorded the violet flash at the cinema, creatures appearing in separate areas and a large red reptile crashing into Coronet Jewelers in EAST.

She knows Elias Trask brought the projector for the Looking Glass Games screening and fled toward his shop halfway along the concourse. She can show her footage, identify evacuation routes and provide a service-pass key.

Police and firefighters arrive roughly ten minutes after the initial alarm and secure the outside approaches. They keep shoppers away from the mall and do not attempt to clear the monster-filled interior. If living monsters run into the parking lot, responders retreat and expand the perimeter; after an hour, the exterior is cordoned off.

entries.name: Looking Glass Games
entries: Halfway along the 450-foot connecting concourse, 225 feet from West Mall, Looking Glass Games occupies a north-side storefront. Its glass displays hold painted miniature dragons, fantasy heroes, polyhedral dice, and books filled with pictures of creatures the adventurers know. The shop doors are open.

READ ALOUD: Behind a shop window, tiny warriors face a painted dragon on a miniature battlefield. Shelves of oddly familiar monsters and illustrated spellcasters stand beside glittering many-sided stones. A man at the door sees your equipment and calls, 'Wait! Are you the ones who came through the movie screen?'

Elias Trask owns Looking Glass Games. He bought the antique crystal projector at an estate sale and installed it for a promotional fantasy-film screening in the West cinema booth. The machine began throwing violet light, people panicked, and Elias fled here. He thinks he caused the disaster and wants it stopped.

Elias installed the projector in WEST cinema booth C3–E4 and knows its RUN/STOP controls. He tried cutting the power after the surge, but its violet light persisted. His phone video from the booth shows eight narrow violet threads leaving the crystal in separate directions, apart from the beam aimed at the screen. He does not understand the threads. He is afraid to return alone but will accompany an escort to the booth.
The window display of painted dragons, fantasy heroes and rulebooks resembles the adventurers' own world. Elias spots their armor and calls from the shop doorway.

SHOP CHARACTER: Looking Glass Games is a modern Alice-inspired hobby shop. Its chessboard display floor, oversized backward-turning clock, 'CURIOUSER AND CURIOUSER' sign and shelves of painted monsters are ordinary props, not new magical clues or puzzles. It sits midway through the connecting concourse; no additional battle map is required.

entries.name: Encounter 2: Food-Court Menagerie
entries: READ ALOUD: Two six-legged black panthers stalk between overturned tables. Above an abandoned prize kiosk floats a single enormous eye, warning anyone nearby to keep away. A nearly invisible cube of jelly slides out of a kitchen doorway, carrying trays and wrappers in its body. Somewhere behind the food counters, a heavy animal pounds against metal.

EAST placements: Spectator M10, hovering 15 feet above the floor; Displacer Beasts N12–O13 and U10–V11; Gelatinous Cube M19–N20 outside the kitchen doorway. All four were already loose when the characters arrived.

FOOD COURT MINI PULLS: Displacer D1 #140 P18 Front BR; Displacer D2 #105 Dark Wolf proxy P14 Front TL; Spectator #119 Nothic proxy P15 Back BL; Gelatinous Cube #139 P18 Front BL. The two Owlbears (#141 and #135 proxy) remain behind their shutters until they emerge.

The Displacer Beasts stalk fleeing shoppers and armed intruders; they compete for prey rather than acting as a team. The Spectator has claimed the shiny contents of a prize kiosk as its treasure, orders everyone to stay away, and attacks if threatened or robbed. It can be reasoned with. The Cube glides toward movement and anything edible, without tactics. None of these creatures obeys the dragon.

Owlbear O1 is trapped in west kitchen G19–H20 behind a 20-foot security shutter across L/M, rows 19–22. O2 is inside east service AC19–AD20 behind a 10-foot shutter across AB–AC on the boundary of rows 15 and 16. Both are drawn closed on EAST DM/player PNGs, with no side passages to bypass them. AC 19, 100 HP per shutter applies when characters intentionally damage it. The DM narrates repeated pounding and buckling, choosing the moment the metal gives way when dramatic timing and established damage support it; do NOT track a mandatory Owlbear damage-per-round counter. An interrupted or reinforced shutter remains closed if players meaningfully prevented its failure. To open a jammed shutter, Dana's service-pass key releases an emergency control and DC 15 Strength (Athletics) lifts it as an action; without the key, DC 17 Dexterity (Thieves' Tools) bypasses the release first. Other reasonable methods work. The Owlbears act independently rather than on a scripted combat schedule.
Food-court tables and counters provide half cover when they obstruct an attack. The Cube starts outside O1's kitchen, not inside the sealed room.
{@creature Displacer Beast|XMM}; {@creature Spectator|XMM}; {@creature Gelatinous Cube|XMM}

entries.name: Spectator Negotiation and Other Options
entries: The Spectator is possessive of a prize kiosk full of glittering tokens. It wants a defined domain where nobody touches its shiny things. It can be reasoned with, bribed with equally interesting objects, or persuaded that a better secure display exists elsewhere. A specific appealing offer plus DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) normally calms it, but a clever convincing solution can work without a roll. It is not allied to the dragon.

Leading the Spectator outside with its prizes, offering it a shiny cart it can escort outdoors, or using Banishment can disconnect its strand without killing it. Negotiation only within the mall ends hostility but keeps its strand connected until it leaves.

The Gelatinous Cube starts M19–N20 outside the west kitchen. Its slow speed may let players bypass it; the strand stays active until it leaves or dies. It can be contained, lured, fought, or forced outdoors. Do not teleport it toward characters just to create combat.

Tables, shop windows, lights, alarms and sprinklers are ordinary mall fixtures. Sprinkler water is not Fire damage and does not stop the Hydra's head regrowth. Counters provide half cover only when they obstruct attack lines.

entries.name: East Mall Between Battles
entries: Coronet Jewelers X2–AG8: Young Red Dragon at Z4–AA5 among the wrecked displays. A tray of watches lies exposed on the food-court side at AD8–AD9, outside broken frontage AB8–AD8. Eddie waits at AE10 for a chance to snatch it. East public exit is AF12–AG13 (correcting the earlier AG12–AH13 mistake). Elias remains at Looking Glass Games halfway along the main concourse.

The Owlbears claw at their jammed shutters until they escape, then scavenge food. A service corridor offers a defensible place for a one-hour short rest, during which the remaining creatures continue their activities.

entries.caption: Eddie's robbery
rows: Eddie hides while the Displacer Beasts, Spectator or Cube are attacking in the open food court. Once they stop, the Owlbears' noise masks his approach. If the characters engage Owlbears, he acts on his own initiative.

After the immediate food-court predators stop fighting nearby, Eddie waits a few minutes, enters Coronet and steals a tray of watches. The dragon pursues him into the food court; Eddie drops the tray and flees toward an outside exit.
Characters can intercept Eddie, confront the dragon early, or take the treasure themselves. The dragon responds to the threat to its hoard.
Within ten minutes the dragon recovers its watches and returns to Coronet. After an hour, Owlbears may be loose and scavenging; the police have secured the outside approaches.

entries.name: Encounter 3: Owlbears and Dragon
entries: Owlbear O1 begins G19–H20 inside the west kitchen behind the L/M shutter and O2 starts AC19–AD20 inside east service behind the AB–AC north shutter. They pound and rattle the metal until a shutter gives way or a player opens it. Their entrance can coincide with the dragon confrontation when the scene justifies it; there is no mandatory round counter. Honor attempts by players to repair, reinforce, block or open either shutter. Once released, each Owlbear seeks food, defends itself and acts independently of the dragon.

Eddie Vale is a Commoner (AC 10, 4 HP, Speed 30 feet), initially EAST AE10. A watch tray lies at AD8–AD9 just outside Coronet's broken frontage. After nearby threats settle down, Eddie moves to AD9, takes the tray as an object interaction, and runs toward the east exit at AF12–AG13, all using normal speed and actions. The dragon notices the theft and moves from the store through the broken frontage; Eddie has no protected turn, guaranteed escape or free Dash. It may catch, hurt, frighten or kill him. If threatened or frightened, he drops the tray. Optional #069 P09 Back TL represents Eddie in initiative only.

READ ALOUD (when the tray is snatched and the dragon reacts): A man darts from the wrecked jewelry display with a tray of watches. From inside the store comes an enormous roar: 'THIEF!' Glass shatters again as a red dragon surges toward the food court.

The Young Red Dragon (178 HP; Fire immunity; Fire Breath DC 17 Dexterity, 16d6 Fire) begins Z4–AA5 inside Coronet. If Eddie snatches the watch tray, the dragon pursues him through the real broken storefront at AB8–AD8. It may attack and catch Eddie normally. It treats armed intruders who threaten its hoard as rival thieves. If the watches are returned, it might negotiate, attack, or retreat to guard its hoard. No outcomes are forced.

Stopping Eddie before he steals leaves the dragon in Coronet unless another action provokes it. The crystal still points to the dragon. Players can face it, negotiate over its hoard, lure it outside, avoid it, or leave the mall without solving every problem. During a one-hour rest, shutters may buckle and Eddie may attempt theft, but do not guarantee that he survives, escapes or succeeds. Owlbears are never teleported into a fight.
{@creature Young Red Dragon|XMM}; {@creature Owlbear|XMM}; {@creature Commoner|XMM}

entries.name: Finale: Practical Triggers and Positions
entries: OPTIONAL ENTRANCE NARRATION after established pounding: 'Metal tears overhead. With a double crash, both service shutters give way, and two owlbears burst into the food court.' This is an available DM beat when justified, not a mandatory scripted event. It does not override player efforts to keep a shutter closed.

FINAL TACTICAL POSITIONS: Red Dragon #159 Z4–AA5 inside Coronet on Large 2×2 footprint (physical catalog figure is oversized, use 2×2 marker); Owlbear #141 G19–H20 and proxy Owlbear #135 AC19–AD20, each Large 2×2. Coronet's broken south frontage AB8–AD8 allows a direct exit. Spectator is 15 feet aloft at encounter start and atrium ceiling is 35 feet; apply actual line of sight and movement.

The Young Red Dragon has 178 HP, Fire immunity, Fire Breath (30-foot cone, DC 17 Dex, 16d6 Fire, recharge 5–6) and otherwise uses its linked 2024 Monster Manual block. It may recover watches and retreat, threaten intruders, negotiate, pursue Eddie outdoors or fight. Outside the mall its strand disconnects, but the dragon remains alive on Earth.

FINAL MINI PULLS: #141 Owlbear P18 Back TL; #135 Dire Bear proxy P17 Back BL; #159 Red Dragon P21 Back Right (keep to 2×2 game footprint). Eddie #069 P09 Back TL only when tactical tracking is useful. Do not bring figures for noncombat NPCs.

entries.name: The Projector and the Return
entries: Projector in WEST cinema booth C3–E4. Motor and STOP lever function normally, but its crystal projects while linked living monsters remain inside the mall. Eight glowing strands show active links; rotating the crystal gives a direction to each remaining creature.

entries.caption: Crystal feedback
rows: Linked monster alive inside the building or on its roof
Its link glows. STOP halts only the motor; the screen remains unstable.
Linked monster dies, travels off-plane, or exits the exterior walls
Its link darkens. Reentering alive, or returning from banishment inside the mall, immediately reconnects.
Final active link ends with STOP already selected
A doorway back to Thornwatch opens in the cinema screen for 60 seconds, even if the party is in East Mall.
Final link ends while motor is RUNNING
Pull STOP to open the screen portal for 60 seconds.
The party arrives after the one-minute window
With no links active, cycle RUN then STOP again to reopen the doorway for another minute.
A linked creature reenters while portal is open
The returning link collapses the portal. The doorway can be reopened once all links are inactive.
No controlled doorway. Independent planar travel remains possible; motor or housing damage can be repaired.

entries: RETURN READ ALOUD: The screen flickers behind you. A moment later the air smells of pine again, and the Thornwatch arch stands beside the road. Its violet marks fade to ordinary gray stone.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: With all eight strands inactive, STOP opens the cinema passage to Thornwatch for one minute. With no active strands, another RUN/STOP cycle opens a new window if the first closes.
Returning to Thornwatch ends the lights and humming at the old arch. The reeve accepts the account and pays the reward promised in the contract.

Living monsters outside the mall remain dangerous on modern Earth even after their links disconnect. Emergency responders maintain the perimeter whether the party returns to Thornwatch or stays to help.

entries.name: Endings and Fast Rulings
entries: VALID ENDINGS: (A) All strands disconnected, crystal intact and STOP used: screen opens home for one minute; (B) crystal destroyed: no return using this projector, party can be permanently stranded on Earth; (C) some monsters are lured outside: those monsters still exist on Earth, even though their strands go dark; (D) adventurers decline to return: Earth is their new setting. None demands a forced escape or rescue.

QUICK LOCATIONS: booth WEST C3–E4; Hydra WEST L13–N15 (3×3); Spectator EAST M10 at 15 ft; Displacers EAST N12–O13 and U10–V11; Cube EAST M19–N20; Owlbears EAST G19–H20 and AC19–AD20 behind shutters; dragon EAST Z4–AA5; Eddie EAST AE10; watch tray AD8–AD9; east exit AF12–AG13; Looking Glass Games midway down 450-foot link.

QUICK OBJECT / SKILL ANSWERS: Arcana DC 13 explains living strands; crystal AC 13/10 HP; shutters AC 19/100 HP when actively attacked, with DM-directed narrative break timing otherwise; Dana's service-pass unlocks emergency release, DC 15 Athletics to lift; without key, DC 17 Thieves' Tools first. Spectator negotiates for territory and shiny prizes. Thornwatch contract offers 400 gp total for reporting back.

NO MINIATURES FOR PLAYERS OR NONCOMBAT NPCS: DM pulls eight numbered monster minis/proxies only; Eddie #069 is optional for combat movement. The security guard Dana, usher Mel, and Elias do not need minis.

The world's physical rules still apply when players improvise: creatures act on motivations and react to choices. You decide when a believable escalation occurs; you never have to roll invisible shutter damage every round merely to justify a dramatic entrance.
